references.text: The parallel account in Matthew where Jesus sends the demons into the pigs, and the whole herd rushes down a steep bank into the sea.
The parallel account in Mark where the unclean spirits go out and enter the pigs, and the herd rushes down a steep bank into the sea and drowns.
The demons ask Jesus to send them into the herd of pigs, which leads directly to the event in Luke 8:33.
Mark's parallel account where the demons ask to be sent into the pigs.
The preceding verse in Luke that tells about the herd of pigs feeding on the mountain and the demons' request to enter them.
Describes how the unclean spirit had seized the man, providing background for the demons' departure from him in verse 33.
The demons identify themselves as 'Legion' because many demons had entered the man – this explains the scale of what happens when they go out and enter the pigs.
